title: Permanent resident returning from travel
facts: A lawful permanent resident generally presents a valid Permanent Resident Card when seeking admission after temporary foreign travel, subject to immigration rules.
Long absences can raise questions about abandonment of permanent residence and can also affect naturalization continuous-residence requirements.

An absence of more than one year creates additional documentation issues; a reentry permit obtained before departure can help with travel documentation but does not guarantee admission or preserve every naturalization rule.
Permanent residents should distinguish immigration status, travel-document validity and naturalization residence rules.
